chapter: Ellington's later years and Quincy Jones
title: Leaving Ellington for Quincy Jones's Free and Easy in Europe
summary: Tired of traveling, Jackson left Ellington in Europe in October 1959 to join Quincy Jones's musical show with Clark Terry.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: So when I left the band, I didn't leave the band on account of because I didn't like the band. I left the band because I was tired of traveling and I left the band in Europe to go with Quincy Jones because we had a show called Free and Easy and Sammy Davis was supposed to be the star of the show had we had our full run in Europe and come back to the United States. And I knew that if Sammy Davis was going to be the star of the show, I would be in New York for a year, two
-- with any show that Sammy was with. But we stayed over in Europe.

That was 1959. I left him in October and Quincy came over in November. So Clark and I left at the same time. You know, Clark, he used to say all the time, 'I'm going to -- I'll bet I'll be here -- I bet I'll leave before you will.' I said, 'No, you won't.' So we wound up leaving together. And we stayed over in Europe until Quincy came and that's when I made a little record that --
Uh-huh. And Clark worked in the Chat qui Peche Shocky Pairs. Clark worked in the Shocky Pairs until Quincy came.
A little club on Rue de la Houchette.
Uh-huh. Right around the corner off of Place St. Michel.
